provider: Telegram public-channel web CDN (t.me/s preview -> cdnN.telesco.pe) — anonymous reads

free_tier.stated: Not a storage tier. This is the READ path for files already in a public channel. Anonymous, no account, no token, no API key. Scraping the public preview of a channel yields directly-fetchable media URLs for every photo and video post.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: It is still validated (bogus token -> 404, no token -> 404), and one minted token 502'd transiently then recovered, so treat tokens as mint-on-demand, not permanent

egress.terms: Free and unmetered, served by Telegram's own nginx-backed web CDN (Server: nginx/1.30.1, Cache-Control: max-age=10800). Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Accept-Ranges advertised, so range requests and browser fetching work. This is genuinely CDN-friendly: put Cloudflare in front and the origin pull is a plain HTTP GET.

tooling: No client needed. Plain curl. Pattern: GET https://t.me/s/<channel> and regex https://cdn\d\.telesco\.pe/file/<hash>.mp4?token=.. The t.me embed widget (https://t.me/<channel>/<id>?embed=1) exposes a second, tokenless URL form (e.g. cdn4.telesco.pe/file/<long-hash>.jpg) that also serves 200/206 anonymously. Pagination works: ?before=<msg_id> walks arbitrarily far back.
chaining: Iterate channels x ?before pagination. Anonymous scrape rate was tested at 12 requests back-to-back on t.me/s/telegram with 12x HTTP 200. No rate limit encountered. Each channel page yields ~20 messages; a file-storage channel where every post is a 2 GB file would expose all of them this way.

Review HTML never emits a document element. Checked t.

limits_note: CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT, probed: this path exposes PHOTOS and VIDEOS only. The preview HTML never emits a document element. Checked t.me/s/telegram, /durov, /tginfo, /tgbeta, /apkpure_official, /drweb, /securitylab: zero occurrences of tgme_widget_message_document, zero .pdf links. Arbitrary files (zips, parquet, models) are NOT reachable anonymously; only the media Telegram re-encodes for preview. Max observed media size is bounded by what the preview embeds.

reliability_note: Token semantics are weaker than they look, which is good for us: a token minted for one video returned 206 on a completely different file (/file/7fde212b67.mp4 with c01503a63e's token) and on a file from a different channel, so the token is a viewer credential, not a per-file signature. It is still validated (bogus token -> 404, no token -> 404), and one minted token 502'd transiently then recovered, so treat tokens as mint-on-demand, not permanent. cdn2.telesco.pe 302s to another host; cdn1 is the one that serves bytes.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: probe: curl -r 0-2047 -> 206, Content-Range: bytes 0-2047/4843, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * — anonymous partial read works
probe: curl -r 0-1023 ... -> 206, Content-Type: video/mp4, Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/2633811 — anonymous range read of video works
probe: grep tgme_widget_message_document across 7 public channels -> 0 hits; this path carries media only, never arbitrary documents
